description: Two-panel composite figure: composition-parameter plots of Charpy impact absorbed energy (J) for low-density Fe-Mn-Al-C steels, redrawn from two literature sources. (a) plots absorbed energy (y-axis 0-300 J, axis title partly cropped at the top edge) against Mn content (x-axis 17-22 wt.%) for Fe-xMn-2Al-0.45C-0.05Si steel. The upper curve (filled triangles, labelled "0 °C") is almost flat, with markers between the 200 and 300 J gridlines (highest at 19 wt.% Mn); the lower curve (filled diamonds, labelled "-196 °C") rises with Mn content, from just below the 50 J gridline at 17 wt.%, to between the 100 and 150 J gridlines at 19 wt.%, to the 150 J line at 22 wt.%. Two large open downward arrows mark the loss of energy on cooling from 0 °C to -196 °C at the two ends. (b) plots the same quantity (y-axis 0-160 J, steps of 20) against Al content (x-axis 2-9 wt.%) for Fee18MnexAl-0.6C steel: markers at 3, 5 and 8 wt.% Al (the first between the 100 and 120 J lines, the second just above 120 J with an error bar, the third below the 20 J line), joined by arrows labelled "A sluggish increase" (3→5 wt.%) and "A steep decrease" (5→8 wt.%). Together they claim Mn and Al content govern cryogenic impact toughness, Mn having little effect at 0 °C.

subfigures.description: Line plot of Charpy impact absorbed energy (y-axis, 0-300 J, title partly cropped) vs Mn content (x-axis, 17-22 wt.%). Two curves: filled triangles labelled '0 °C', nearly flat with markers between the 200 and 300 J gridlines; filled diamonds labelled '-196 °C', increasing from just below the 50 J gridline (17 wt.% Mn) through a value between the 100 and 150 J gridlines (19 wt.%) to the 150 J line (22 wt.%). Error bars are drawn on several markers, and two large open downward arrows indicate the cryogenic drop.

Line plot of Charpy impact absorbed energy (y-axis 'Charpy impact absorbed energy, J', 0-160 in 20 J steps) vs Al content (x-axis, 2-9 wt.%). Three markers at 3, 5 and 8 wt.% Al: the 3 wt.% point lies between the 100 and 120 J gridlines, the 5 wt.% point just above the 120 J gridline and carries an error bar, the 8 wt.% point lies below the 20 J gridline. A grey arrow labelled 'A sluggish increase' links 3 to 5 wt.% Al; a longer grey arrow labelled 'A steep decrease' links 5 to 8 wt.% Al. No numeric data labels are printed.

observations.observation: Panel (a) shows two Charpy impact absorbed-energy curves for Fe-xMn-2Al-0.45C-0.05Si steel: an upper curve labelled '0 °C' (filled triangles) and a lower curve labelled '-196 °C' (filled diamonds), plotted against Mn content from 17 to 22 wt.% on a 0-300 J y-axis.
In panel (a) the '0 °C' curve is essentially flat: its markers all lie between the 200 and 300 J gridlines, with the maximum at 19 wt.% Mn.

In panel (a) the '-196 °C' curve increases with Mn content: the marker at 17 wt.% Mn sits just below the 50 J gridline, the 19 wt.% marker lies between the 100 and 150 J gridlines, and the 22 wt.% marker lies on the 150 J line.
Two large open downward arrows in panel (a) mark the vertical drop in absorbed energy between the 0 °C and -196 °C conditions at about 17 wt.% Mn and at 22 wt.% Mn.
Panel (b) plots Charpy impact absorbed energy (0-160 J, 20 J ticks) against Al content (2-9 wt.%) with single data points at 3, 5 and 8 wt.% Al, the 5 wt.% point carrying the only visible error bar.
Panel (b) annotates the 3 to 5 wt.% Al segment with a short arrow labelled 'A sluggish increase' and the 5 to 8 wt.% Al segment with a long arrow labelled 'A steep decrease'.
The caption states that panel (a) gives the Charpy impact absorbed energy of Fe-xMn-2Al-0.45C-0.05Si steel as a function of Mn content and cites ref. [101].
The caption states that panel (b) gives the Charpy impact absorbed energy of Fee18MnexAl-0.6C steel as a function of Al content and cites ref. [102].

The citing text reports cryogenic impact energies of 80.5, 49.8 and 41.1 J for 17, 19 and 22 wt.% Mn respectively; this decreasing trend disagrees with the rising '-196 °C' markers visible in panel (a), so the two readings are reported as conflicting.
The citing text reports cryogenic ductility values of 75.7%, 53.4% and 9.7% for the 17, 19 and 22 wt.% Mn steels; these values are not printed in the figure.
The citing text states that the impact energy at cryogenic temperature increased from 122 to 138 J when Al content increased from 3 to 5 wt.%, values not printed on panel (b).
The citing text states that the influences of Mn content on tensile and Charpy impact properties at room temperature were minimal, consistent with the flat '0 °C' curve in panel (a).
The y-axis title of panel (a) is partly cropped at the top edge of the image and is not fully legible; panel (b) carries the full title 'Charpy impact absorbed energy, J'.
